draftA:
REQ-1: Before a full application, the loan app must run a pre-qualification check that returns a likely/not-likely result within seconds and states it is not a final decision.
REQ-2: Debt-to-income is (all existing monthly debt payments + the new loan's monthly payment) divided by gross monthly income; the result must be at most 43% to pass.
REQ-3: Credit score must be at least 640 to pass; v1 uses only these two factors (DTI and credit score) and no others.
REQ-4: A not-likely result must name the specific failing factor in plain words, with the applicant's own figure and the limit, and repeat that this is not a final decision.
AC-1: Gross monthly income 5,000; existing debt payments 1,500; new loan payment 600 -> 2,100/5,000 = 42%, at or under 43%, credit score 700 >= 640 -> result: likely to qualify.
AC-2: Gross monthly income 5,000; existing debt 1,600; new loan payment 600 -> 2,200/5,000 = 44%, above 43% -> not likely, message: "Your total monthly debt, including this loan, would be 44% of your gross monthly income. Our limit is 43%. This is not a final decision."
AC-3: DTI 30% (passes) but credit score 639 -> not likely, message: "Your credit score is 639. We require at least 640. This is not a final decision."
AC-4: Boundary case: DTI exactly 43% and credit score exactly 640 -> likely to qualify, since both thresholds are inclusive.
draftB:
REQ-1: Before a full application, tell a personal-loan applicant in seconds whether they are likely to qualify, and why.
REQ-2: Use only debt-to-income and credit score: total monthly debt, including the new loan payment, at most 43% of gross monthly income, and a credit score of at least 640.
REQ-3: If not likely to qualify, show the specific reason in plain words and state that this is not a final decision.
AC-1: Gross monthly income 5000, total monthly debt including the new payment 2150, score 640: likely to qualify, because debt is exactly 43% and the score meets 640.
AC-2: Gross monthly income 5000, total monthly debt including the new payment 2151, score 700: not likely to qualify because debt is over 43% of gross income; state this is not a final decision.
AC-3: Gross monthly income 4000, total monthly debt including the new payment 1720, score 639: not likely to qualify because the score is below 640; state this is not a final decision.

reviewOfA.strengths: The DTI examples recompute exactly (2,100/5,000 = 42% and 2,200/5,000 = 44%), and the inclusive 43% and 640 cutoffs match the stated at-most and at-least rules.

findings.title: No rule when both checks fail
findings.detail: Nothing states what an applicant sees when debt-to-income exceeds 43% and the score is under 640. The requester required the specific reason; with no rule, one reason may be hidden, making the explanation incomplete or inconsistent.
findings.quote: REQ-3: If not likely to qualify, show the specific reason in plain words and state that this is not a final decision.

findings.title: New loan payment source undefined
findings.detail: The rule depends on the new loan's monthly payment, but the draft never says how that payment is obtained (requested amount, term, rate). Without it the check cannot be computed or tested consistently.
findings.quote: total monthly debt, including the new loan payment, at most 43% of gross monthly income

findings.title: No test for invalid income
findings.detail: Zero, missing or non-numeric income would make the ratio undefined. No requirement or acceptance criterion covers input validation, so behaviour at the division step is unspecified.
findings.quote: AC-1: Gross monthly income 5000, total monthly debt including the new payment 2150, score 640: likely to qualify

findings.title: Likely-qualify reason and speed untested
findings.detail: REQ-1 promises a result in seconds and an explanation, but no acceptance criterion checks response time or the reason shown to an applicant who is likely to qualify. Only decline reasons are tested.
findings.quote: REQ-1: Before a full application, tell a personal-loan applicant in seconds whether they are likely to qualify, and why.

reviewOfB.strengths: The three acceptance criteria are arithmetically correct and well chosen: 2150 is exactly 43% of 5000, 2151 is just over, and 1720 is exactly 43% of 4000, cleanly testing the boundary of each rule.

merge.document:
REQ-1: Before a full application, the loan app runs a pre-qualification check that returns a likely/not-likely result within seconds, says why, and states it is not a final decision.
REQ-2: Debt-to-income = (existing monthly debt payments + the new loan's monthly payment) divided by gross monthly income; at most 43% passes (43% itself passes).
REQ-3: Credit score must be at least 640 to pass (640 itself passes). v1 uses only these two factors and no others.
REQ-4: Likely to qualify only if both checks pass.
REQ-5: A not-likely result names every failing factor in plain words, with the applicant's own figure and the limit, and repeats that this is not a final decision; if both fail, both reasons are shown.
REQ-6: The new loan's monthly payment is an input to the check, derived from the requested amount and term before the ratio is computed; the check cannot run without it.
REQ-7: If gross monthly income is missing, zero or non-numeric, or the new loan's payment is unavailable, no result is given; the app asks for the missing input. This is not a decline.
AC-1: Gross monthly income 5,000; existing debt 1,500; new loan payment 600 -> 2,100/5,000 = 42%, credit score 700 -> likely to qualify, shown with the reason that debt is 42% of gross income (limit 43%) and the score meets 640.
AC-2: Gross monthly income 5,000; total debt including the new payment 2,150 (43% exactly); score 640 -> likely to qualify; both thresholds are inclusive.
AC-3: Gross monthly income 5,000; existing debt 1,600; new loan payment 600 -> 2,200/5,000 = 44%; score 700 -> not likely: "Your total monthly debt, including this loan, would be 44% of your gross monthly income. Our limit is 43%. This is not a final decision."
AC-4: Gross monthly income 5,000; total debt including the new payment 2,151 -> 43.02%, above 43% -> not likely for debt-to-income; states this is not a final decision.
AC-5: Gross monthly income 4,000; total debt including the new payment 1,720 (43% exactly); score 639 -> not likely: "Your credit score is 639. We require at least 640. This is not a final decision."
AC-6: Debt-to-income 44% and credit score 639 -> not likely, both reasons shown with figures and limits, plus the not-a-final-decision line.
AC-7: Gross monthly income 0, missing or non-numeric -> no ratio is computed and no result is returned; the app asks for a valid gross monthly income.
AC-8: Response time: for each case above, the result and reason appear within seconds of submission.
Open question for the credit risk lead: how the new loan's monthly payment is calculated (amount, term, rate), since the brief does not state it.
merge.keptFromA: Draft A's explicit DTI formula, inclusive 43%/640 thresholds, the verified 42%/44% worked examples and the plain-words decline wording with the applicant's own figure and the limit.
merge.keptFromB: Draft B's exact-boundary acceptance criteria (2,150 of 5,000 and 1,720 of 4,000 are both exactly 43%, 2,151 just over) and its compact phrasing of the two-factor rule.

resolutions.finding: Review of draft A: no defects found
resolutions.note: Rejected as incomplete: draft A shares draft B's gaps (no rule when both checks fail, no source for the new loan payment, no invalid-income handling, no speed or likely-case test). These are fixed in REQ-5 to REQ-7 and AC-6 to AC-8, so draft A's content is kept but extended.

resolutions.finding: D-B1 P1 No rule when both checks fail
resolutions.note: REQ-5 now requires every failing factor to be named, and AC-6 tests 44% DTI with a 639 score showing both reasons.

resolutions.finding: D-B2 P1 New loan payment source undefined
resolutions.note: REQ-6 makes the new loan's monthly payment a required input derived from requested amount and term before the ratio; the exact calculation is not in the given facts, so it is listed as an open question rather than invented.

resolutions.finding: D-B3 P2 No test for invalid income
resolutions.note: REQ-7 specifies no result and a request for a valid figure when income is zero, missing or non-numeric, and AC-7 tests it; it is explicitly not a decline.

resolutions.finding: D-B4 P2 Likely-qualify reason and speed untested
resolutions.note: AC-1 now checks the reason shown to a likely applicant, and AC-8 checks that every case returns within seconds.
